title: Chen Dynasty
capsule: The Chen dynasty (557–589) was the fourth and last of the Southern Dynasties in the period of division following the Han, founded by the general Chen Baxian, who overthrew the weakened Liang dynasty and proclaimed himself Emperor Wu in 557. The dynasty controlled the Yangtze River basin and south China but was the smallest and weakest of the Southern Dynasties, hemmed in by the Northern Zhou and later Northern Qi in the north. Its last emperor, Chen Shubao (r. 582–589), was notorious for dissolute rule; when the Sui emperor Yang Jian launched a massive southern campaign in 588–589, the Chen collapsed with minimal resistance, and Yang Jian's conquest in early 589 unified China for the first time since the Western Jin, ending over three centuries of division.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The broad extent of Chen territory in south China is known from dynastic histories, but precise northern frontier delineation fluctuated with Sui-Chen military interaction and is approximated in mapping.
